findings.issue: Children can go untraced without anything noticing, and it happens in the suite this tool is built for. The hook reaches a child only as the FIRST `sitecustomize` on PYTHONPATH. tests/test_drive_phase.py's `_pinned_clock` (line 286) and `_windows_stdout` (line 313) put a fixture directory holding its own `sitecustomize.py` ahead of it. Python imports only one `sitecustomize`, and the fixture's does not chain, so every drive-phase.py verb child started inside those blocks runs untraced at BOTH revisions. Those verbs are the stamped and CRLF routes: `_pinned_clock(` appears 5 times and `_windows_stdout(` twice, at both 92c399f5 and HEAD. The tool cannot detect this. The empty-reach refusal is per revision (line 522), and the printed `processes traced` counts only processes that dumped (read_traces, line 363). A child that never ran the hook, or ran it and ended through os._exit or a kill, is in no number. The counts also cannot separate 'fewer processes because drives were converted', which is the expected effect of the conversions this tool gates, from 'processes untraced'. A conversion at P152.4, P152.11 or P152.13 that drops a pinned-clock drive loses lines that were never in the base reach, and the tool exits 0. The docstring lists 'another sitecustomize earlier on its path' generically, but neither the docstring nor the filed outcome says that the target suite has that shape.
findings.resolution: Also write the hook as `usercustomize.py` in the same directory, guarded so it installs once per process. site.py imports usercustomize independently of which sitecustomize won wherever user site is enabled; say where it is not (-s, PYTHONNOUSERSITE, a venv without system site). Have the hook write a start marker when it installs. read_traces then prints started against dumped per revision, which makes os._exit and kills visible, plus a count of processes reached only through the usercustomize entry, which makes shadowing visible. Add a selftest case whose fixture suite starts the module's child under a non-chaining `sitecustomize` planted first on PYTHONPATH, and assert that the child's lines are measured. Prove it red against the current single entry point.

findings.file: tools/reach-diff.py:252-253,533 (gone excluded from the exit code); docstring 46-52
findings.issue: contradicts task clause 'prints every line reached at the base revision and not reached at the head revision ... exit 1 when any such line exists and 0 otherwise'. A base-reached line whose (function, text, occurrence) key the head module no longer holds is listed as `gone` and never decides the exit code (`result["code"] = 1 if found["gaps"] else 0`). So when a conversion renames a function, or extracts a planner and moves lines out of a route function, every moved line the head suite no longer reaches leaves the exit code 0. Its text can still be in the module, unreached. The gates P152.4, P152.11 and P152.13 read the exit code, so this is a pass that measured a loss. rd16 pins the reworded-and-still-reached case. No case covers moved-to-another-function-and-unreached.
findings.resolution: Before declaring a key gone, match it again by (stripped text, occurrence in the whole module) at the head. A match the head did not reach is a gap, which exits 1. Only text the head module no longer holds anywhere stays `gone`. Add a fixture tag that moves `return "positive"` into a renamed helper and drops its case, and assert exit 1. Alternatively, if `gone` is meant to stay non-deciding, amend the task description and the CONTRIBUTING bullet to say so. The current code does not do what the clause asked.

findings.issue: A lost line can hide behind an identical line in the same function whenever the module changes in that function, and this is neither documented nor tested. `occurrence` counts the earlier identical lines in the function. Inserting or removing one identical line above (`return 0`, `return code`, `continue`; the short route lines this tool exists to keep reached) shifts every later occurrence. Example: base f reaches A=`return 0` (occ0) and B=`return 0` (occ1). The head adds N=`return 0` above both, so N is occ0, A is occ1 and B is occ2, and the head reaches N and A. Base occ0 matches N and base occ1 matches A, both reached. B's loss is hidden and the exit is 0. When the module is byte-identical, as drive-phase.py was in the executor's real run, keys coincide and nothing hides. A conversion that also edits the module is exposed. rd10 proves only that two occurrences are distinct keys, not that an insertion leaves them stable.
findings.resolution: Align the base and head lines of each function with difflib.SequenceMatcher over stripped text instead of an occurrence index, so an inserted or deleted duplicate does not renumber the others. Add a fixture tag that inserts an identical earlier line and drops reach to the later one, and assert exit 1 naming it. At minimum, state the limitation in the docstring's matching section.

findings.issue: The bullet says the tool 'exits 1 naming each line of the module reached before and not after' and that the tracer runs 'in every Python process the suite starts'. Both overclaim. Reached lines whose function or text changed are listed as gone and leave it at 0 (finding 2), and children behind a non-chaining sitecustomize are not traced (finding 1). The pointer to the docstring for what the tracer cannot see is present, but the sentence itself states the stronger claim.
findings.resolution: Say that lines whose function or text changed are listed apart as gone and do not fail it, unless finding 2 is fixed. Replace 'in every Python process' with 'in every Python process that imports its hook', next to the existing docstring pointer.

findings.issue: The tool changes the route of the run it measures. Its hook directory holds a `sitecustomize.py` on PYTHONPATH, and `_needs_process()` returns True for any PYTHONPATH entry holding one. Under reach-diff, every verb tests/test_drive_phase.py would run in-process therefore runs as a process: that accounts for the thousands of traced processes and the 717 s wall in the real run. drive-phase.py's real `run_verb` subprocess route is then reached because of the tool, not the suite. The effect is the same at both revisions, so it creates no false gap while the routing stays the same. It is still a measured reach that differs from what the sweep runs, and nothing says so.
findings.resolution: The usercustomize entry from finding 1 also removes this, because the detector looks only for sitecustomize.py. Otherwise, name this effect in the docstring's WHAT IT CANNOT SEE section.

intent.note: Clause 'runs the suite's blocks (each STAGES block, or the whole file) at each revision in a scratch export with a line tracer restricted to that module's code objects': matches. suite_blocks/_measure run one job per STAGES label through the sweep's run_one, and the hook's `ours()` keeps only code whose resolved co_filename is the export's module. Clause 'prints every line reached at the base revision and not reached at the head revision, grouped by enclosing function, exit 1 when any such line exists and 0 otherwise': diverges. Line 533 `result["code"] = 1 if found["gaps"] else 0` excludes `gone`, which is base-reached lines whose key the head lacks, so moving a line into another function and leaving it unreached exits 0 (finding 2). Clause 'a line that moved is matched by its function and text, not its number': matches for moves within a function (line_keys/reach_gaps; rd2, rd3, rd11), with the occurrence-shift gap in finding 3. Clause 'It never writes the checkout': matches. It uses git archive into a mkdtemp removed in finally, registers no worktree (`git worktree list` shows none), and rd15 holds it. Clause 'Its own --selftest proves both directions ... dropping the only case that reaches a branch goes red and names the line; a pure refactor that only moves code stays green': matches (rd1 against rd2/rd3, where rd3 shows the reached line numbers differ). Clause 'CONTRIBUTING.md: one paragraph where test conversions are described': matches. CONTRIBUTING had no paragraph on conversions; the bullet sits under the selftest rule and carries no number. The executor's outcome does describe this diff, including that `gone` 'do[es] not decide the exit code' and the 16 cases (my run of the gate printed `1/1 files ok, 16 cases`, exit 0). It omits that the target suite's `_pinned_clock`/`_windows_stdout` children are shadowed from the hook (finding 1).
